title: How much dimension does an epsilon-approximation to a non-attained quantum correlation cost? A Diophantine answer for K_5
description: The Dykema-Paulsen-Prakash proof that C_q(5,2) is not closed, via a K_5 graph correlation function, is existential in dimension: the finite-dimensional carriers it invokes live in M_k 'for some natural number k', with no control on k and no approximating sequence, rate or carrier at the non-attained parameter. This paper answers the quantitative question that leaves open. Writing D(eps) for the least block dimension of a finite-dimensional carrier whose value exceeds the infimum by at most eps, at exact marginals and at t = 1/sqrt(5), it proves D(eps) = Theta(eps^(-1/4)) and shows the exponent is arithmetic rather than dynamical in origin. The lower bound (Theorem A) is unconditional, with no block-scalar or equal-rank hypothesis: it runs the Diophantine inequality ||q sqrt(5)|| > 1/(5q) through the law of total variance, giving Q eps^(1/4) > 0.4472135955. The upper bound (Theorem B) is attained along an explicit family of two-block carriers built from consecutive continued-fraction convergents of sqrt(5), where the deficit is exactly the product of the two one-sided approximation errors, giving N eps^(1/4) -> 0.9732489895. The constant is therefore bracketed to a factor 2.176 in the denominator convention - a bracket, not a pin, since D is a minimum over all carriers. Two structural results accompany the law: orbit topology and attainment are different invariants on this object (lambda = 4/3 is attained and has an orbit conjugate to that of the unattained sqrt(5), with the same multiplier), and the analogous cost for I3322 is only logarithmic, so dimension laws for non-closure witnesses are governed by the arithmetic of the parameter and not by a universal rate. Three stdlib-only exact-arithmetic engines certify every numbered arithmetic claim (48 + 6 + 4 assertions, exit 0); the load-bearing table is certified by two engines sharing no number representation, with the one shared ingredient disclosed. Version 1.0.2 settles the drift regime (marginals allowed to move by delta): against the fixed target the cost is D(eps, delta) = Theta(min(eps^(-1/4), delta^(-1/4))), the same fourth root, and the delta^(-1/2) conjectured as an Open Lemma in v1.0.0-1.0.1 is refuted by an explicit two-block carrier at denominator 17 whose deficit is exactly zero with marginals off by 6e-7; the conjectured form survives only for a deficit referenced to the carrier's own mean. The complete refereeing record - two refutation-first blind rounds either side of a repair round, with mutation testing and freeze checks - ships in-repository under review/.
